newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Self-confessed Srebrenica killer to stand trial.
newsitem.headline: Self-confessed Srebrenica killer to stand trial.

text.p: A young Bosnian Croat who confessed to taking part in a massacre of Bosnian Moslems at Srebrenica in July 1995 will stand trial next month, the U.N. criminal tribunal for former Yugoslavia said on Monday.
Drazen Erdemovic, 24, pleaded guilty on May 31 to helping shoot dead hundreds of unarmed Moslem men after the U.N. protected "safe area" fell to Bosnian Serb forces.
He wept as he told the tribunal that officers of the Bosnian Serb army unit he was serving in at the time had said he too would be shot if he refused to take part in the killings.
Erdemovic was arrested in Serbia and transferred to the U.N. tribunal's detention centre earlier this year after speaking to Western media about his role in the Srebrenica killings.

He was originally scheduled to have attended a two-day pre-sentencing hearing in July, but this was postponed because experts had concluded he was suffering from post-traumatic stress and therefore could not stand trial.

The tribunal said on Monday that a panel of three independent experts had since concluded that Erdemovic was able to stand trial and that the pre-sentencing hearing would now take place on November 19 and 20.
As Erdemovic has already pleaded guilty, the hearings will be limited to a consideration of possible mitigating or aggravating circumstances, followed by sentencing.
Tribunal sources have said the judges are likely to view his cooperation with the prosecutor's office as a mitigating factor.
Erdemovic is believed to have provided tribunal prosecutors with important evidence about the alleged killing of thousands of Moslems men at Srebrenica.
Deposed Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic and Bosnian Serb military commander General Ratko Mladic have been charged with genocide over Srebrenica, but both men remain free.
